context: Sho-young joins a kid baseball team; Daichi cheers him on.
purpose: Father supporting child during first organized sport.

lines.speaker: sho_child
lines.jp: お父さん、試合、緊張する!
lines.en: Dad, I'm nervous about the match…
lines.style: Quick intake of breath, voice a bit higher with worry. Soft, honest confession — not dramatizing. The vulnerability of admitting fear to someone he trusts. Slight tremor in 'nervous' then steadies himself.

lines.speaker: daichi_kansai
lines.en: Yeah, you sound like a real player!
lines.style: Warm Kansai lilt on the opening. Playful encouragement — not dismissing the nerves but reframing them. Gentle, proud tone. A father noticing his son's seriousness and meeting it with lightness.

lines.speaker: sho_child
lines.en: Will I be able to do it okay?
lines.style: Smaller voice now. Hesitant, searching upward at the end — not quite a question mark, more like checking in. The worry sitting just under the surface. Soft and trusting.

lines.speaker: daichi_kansai
lines.jp: 練習通り、頑張ったらええ。
lines.en: Just do what you practiced — that's all you need.
lines.style: Steady, quiet reassurance. Kansai warmth underneath. Not lecturing — offering a practical truth. The tone of someone who's seen a child's doubt and knows exactly what to say. Slight emphasis on 'practiced'.

lines.speaker: sho_child
lines.style: Urgency underneath the politeness. The 'please' carries weight — this matters. Eyes probably up. Soft but clear. Needing confirmation. Hopeful but not quite certain he'll get it.

lines.speaker: daichi_kansai
lines.en: I'll be right there watching the whole time.
lines.style: Firm Kansai reassurance. The kind of promise a parent makes when they mean it completely. Warm, steady, no room for doubt. Almost protective in its certainty.

lines.speaker: sho_child
lines.style: The nervousness shifts into determination. A bright upturn on the opening. Small voice but not small courage. The moment he leaves the safety of his father's presence and steps into the match. Forward momentum.
